text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central bank probes how unauthenticated report on the economy was released to the press without clearance, deputy governor Victor Odozi says.
- Central bank official arrested over 1.1 billion naira fraud involving the Federal Environmental Protection Agency.
- Another human head linked to ritual murders found in a hotel in eastern Nigeria, police say.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha says Nigerians must focus on wealth creation rather than wealth sharing if the nation's resources are not to be prematurely exhausted.
- Twenty five officers of the anti-narcotics agency arrested over missing luggage at northern Kano airport.
- We won't quit Nigeria, says U.S. oil giant Mobil in paid advert in the American Time magazine.

- U.S. ambassador in Nigeria Walter Carrington says Washington is impressed by on-going economic policies of the military government but warns that continued detention of opposition figures could lead to stiffer sanctions on Nigeria.
